basis: Protein-misfolding amyloidosis; renal medullary abnormalities and creatinine elevation in 80-99%. Cardiac amyloid is 1-4%; ventricular dysfunction does not establish direct cardiac deposition.

decisions.renal: involved: renal medullary disease and impaired renal function occur in 80-99%; renal injury is the dominant manifestation of this protein-defined amyloidosis.

basis: Sensory/autonomic neuropathy with defining chronic intestinal dysmotility. Fractures and wounds are secondary injuries; hyperhidrosis alone is not skin damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: gastrointestinal dysfunction is explicit in the definition and synonyms; intestinal dysmotility is a defining loss of digestive function.

basis: Severe neurodevelopmental disease; vesicoureteral reflux and gingival overgrowth each 2/4. Neonatal distress alone does not establish lung damage; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.

decisions.pulmonary: none: neonatal respiratory distress (4/4) alone does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage; tracheomalacia and laryngomalacia are each reported in only 1/4.

basis: Follicular hyperkeratosis and scarring alopecia define the disease; explicit polyamine-metabolism ancestry supports a metabolic axis. Corneal dystrophy and blepharitis occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the explicit parent 'disorder of polyamine metabolism' supports classification as a metabolic disorder, beyond the cutaneous phenotype.

basis: Defining popliteal skin webs, syndactyly and contractures accompany oral clefts and lower-lip pits. Genital malformations have no applicable axis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: congenital cutaneous webbing behind the knees is the named pterygium and a defining structural skin abnormality.

basis: Skeletal fusions and contractures define the syndrome together with cutaneous pterygia; webbed neck occurs in 5/9. Cleft palate occurs in only 1/10.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: pterygia are defining congenital skin webs; webbed neck is present in 5/9, supporting cutaneous involvement beyond uncommon antecubital webs.

basis: Brain, skeletal and ear/hearing abnormalities characterize the syndrome; renal hypoplasia occurs in 6/6. Four-axis cap; lesser cutaneous and oral anomalies omitted.

decisions.otologic: primary: congenital ear abnormalities and hearing loss are characteristic components of van Maldergem syndrome; hearing impairment is reported in 3/3.

basis: ATP synthase deficiency; encephalopathy, seizures and cerebellar hypoplasia each 2/2; pulmonary hypoplasia 2/2. Nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: this is defined by mitochondrial ATP synthase deficiency; encephalopathy, seizures and cerebellar hypoplasia each affect 2/2 reported patients.

basis: Contractures and skin hyalinosis define disease; immunodeficiency/thymic hypoplasia and GI malabsorption each 80-99%. Adrenal abnormalities lack demonstrated functional damage.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: immunodeficiency and thymic aplasia/hypoplasia are each reported in 80-99%; the mechanism axis is added whenever immunodeficiency applies.

basis: Eye, palate and cerebral abnormalities define syndrome; nail aplasia/hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Asthma is separately diagnosed; joint laxity and small extremities do not establish skeletal damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: asthma, despite an 80-99% annotation, is a separately diagnosed airway disease; direct pulmonary involvement by this malformation syndrome is not established.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: nail aplasia/hypoplasia is direct structural loss of a cutaneous appendage, reported in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility, small hands and short feet (30-79%) do not by themselves establish skeletal injury or loss of function.
